subject: Franska
title: Grammar: passé composé
sourceSummary: How the passé composé is formed with avoir or être, and the most common past participle forms.

questions.prompt: How is the passé composé formed in French?
questions.opener: Two parts: an auxiliary verb and the participle.
choices: Just with avoir, at the end
Participle conjugated + avoir at the end
questions.explanation: The passé composé is formed with avoir or être conjugated in the present tense, followed by the participle: "J'ai mangé."

questions.prompt: Choose the right auxiliary verb: "Je ___ allé à Paris." (aller = movement)
questions.opener: Verbs describing movement from one place to another use être.
questions.explanation: Verbs describing motion/movement (aller, partir, venir) use "être" as the auxiliary: "je suis allé".

questions.prompt: Choose the right auxiliary verb: "Nous ___ mangé une pizza." (manger = to eat)
questions.opener: Most verbs that do NOT describe movement use avoir.
questions.explanation: "Manger" doesn't describe movement, so it uses "avoir": "nous avons mangé".

questions.prompt: Which participle belongs to "faire" (to do/make)? An irregular verb.
questions.opener: One of the most common irregular participles.
questions.explanation: "Faire" has the irregular participle "fait": "j'ai fait mes devoirs" (I have done my homework).

questions.prompt: Write the participle of "finir" (to finish) — a regular -ir verb.
Correct the error: "Hier j'ai allé en ville." (Yesterday I went downtown.)
questions.answer: Hier je suis allé(e) en ville.
steps: "Aller" (to go) describes movement, so the auxiliary should be "être", not "avoir".
With être, the participle must also agree with the subject's gender: "allé" (boy) or "allée" (girl). Full sentence: "Hier je suis allé(e) en ville."

questions.prompt: How is the passé composé formed in French, and when do you use avoir versus être?
questions.opener: Two auxiliary verbs and two kinds of participles.
questions.answer: Structure: avoir/être (present tense) + participle. Être is used for movement: aller → suis allé(e), partir → suis parti(e), venir → suis venu(e) — the participle then agrees with the subject's gender/number. Avoir is used for most other verbs: manger → ai mangé, parler → ai parlé, finir → ai fini. Irregular participles: fait (faire), eu (avoir), été (être), vu (voir), pris (prendre).
